name: O-Level Physics
constants: g = 10 N kg⁻¹ · Speed of light in vacuum = 3.0 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ · Specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J kg⁻¹ °C⁻¹ · Density of water = 1000 kg m⁻³

questions.q: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 2.0 m s⁻² for 5.0 s. What is its final speed?
questions.x: v = u + at = 0 + 2.0 × 5.0 = 10 m s⁻¹. 25 is the distance travelled in metres, not the speed.

questions.q: A stone is dropped from rest. Air resistance is negligible. How far does it fall during the third second of its fall?
questions.x: Distance after 3 s = ½ × 10 × 3² = 45 m; after 2 s = ½ × 10 × 2² = 20 m. During the third second it falls 45 − 20 = 25 m.

questions.q: A spacecraft far from any planet or star is moving with its engines switched off. How does it move?
o: It moves at constant speed in a straight line.
questions.x: With no resultant force, Newton's first law says an object keeps moving at constant velocity. No force is needed to keep it moving.

questions.q: A 2.0 kg box is pulled across a floor by a horizontal force of 10 N. The friction on the box is 4.0 N. What is its acceleration?
questions.x: Resultant force = 10 − 4.0 = 6.0 N, so a = F/m = 6.0/2.0 = 3.0 m s⁻². Using 10 N alone ignores friction and gives 5.0 m s⁻².

questions.q: A uniform metre rule is balanced at its midpoint. A 3.0 N weight hangs 20 cm to the left of the pivot. How far to the right of the pivot must a 4.0 N weight hang to balance the rule?
questions.x: Principle of moments: 3.0 × 20 = 4.0 × d, so d = 60/4.0 = 15 cm. The heavier weight sits closer to the pivot.

questions.q: A uniform plank 2.0 m long weighs 100 N. It rests on a pivot 0.50 m from end P. What downward force at P keeps the plank horizontal?
questions.x: The weight acts at the centre, 1.0 m from P, which is 0.50 m beyond the pivot. Moments: F × 0.50 = 100 × 0.50, so F = 100 N.

questions.q: A person of weight 600 N stands on a floor. The total area of the soles of their shoes is 0.030 m². What pressure do they exert on the floor?
questions.x: p = F/A = 600/0.030 = 20 000 Pa. Multiplying instead of dividing gives 18 Pa.

questions.q: Atmospheric pressure is 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa. What is the total pressure on a diver 5.0 m below the surface of fresh water?
questions.x: Pressure due to water = hρg = 5.0 × 1000 × 10 = 5.0 × 10⁴ Pa. Add atmospheric pressure: 1.0 × 10⁵ + 0.5 × 10⁵ = 1.5 × 10⁵ Pa.

questions.q: A 0.50 kg ball is dropped from a height of 20 m. Air resistance is negligible. What is its speed just before it hits the ground?
questions.x: Loss in GPE = gain in KE: mgh = ½mv², so v = √(2gh) = √(2 × 10 × 20) = √400 = 20 m s⁻¹. The mass cancels.

questions.q: An electric motor lifts a 50 kg load through 12 m in 20 s. The electrical power input to the motor is 500 W. What is the efficiency of the motor?
questions.x: Useful work = mgh = 50 × 10 × 12 = 6000 J, so useful power = 6000/20 = 300 W. Efficiency = 300/500 = 60 %.

questions.q: By which process can thermal energy travel through a vacuum?
questions.x: Radiation is carried by infrared electromagnetic waves, which need no medium. Conduction and convection both need particles.

questions.q: 0.20 kg of water at 80 °C is mixed with 0.30 kg of water at 20 °C. No heat is lost to the surroundings. What is the final temperature?
questions.x: Heat lost = heat gained: 0.20 × (80 − T) = 0.30 × (T − 20), so 16 − 0.20T = 0.30T − 6 and T = 22/0.50 = 44 °C. 50 °C would be the answer only for equal masses.

questions.q: A wave has a frequency of 50 Hz and a wavelength of 0.40 m. What is its speed?
Which of these electromagnetic waves has the longest wavelength?
questions.x: In order of increasing wavelength: gamma rays, X-rays, ultraviolet, visible light, infrared, microwaves, radio waves.

questions.q: A ray of light passes from air into glass of refractive index 1.5. The angle of incidence is 30°. What is the angle of refraction?
questions.x: n = sin i / sin r, so sin r = sin 30° / 1.5 = 0.50/1.5 = 0.333 and r = 19°. Dividing the angle itself by 1.5 gives 20°, which is wrong.

questions.q: What is the critical angle for light in glass of refractive index 1.5?
A 6.0 Ω resistor and a 3.0 Ω resistor are connected in parallel. What is their combined resistance?
questions.x: 1/R = 1/6.0 + 1/3.0 = 3/6.0, so R = 2.0 Ω. A parallel combination is always smaller than its smallest resistor. 9.0 Ω is the series total.

questions.q: A 12 V battery of negligible internal resistance is connected to a 4.0 Ω resistor in series with a parallel pair of 6.0 Ω and 3.0 Ω resistors. What is the current in the 6.0 Ω resistor?
questions.x: The parallel pair is 2.0 Ω, so the total is 6.0 Ω and I = 12/6.0 = 2.0 A. The p.d. across the pair is 2.0 × 2.0 = 4.0 V, so the 6.0 Ω resistor carries 4.0/6.0 = 0.67 A. The 3.0 Ω resistor carries 1.3 A.

questions.q: Which material is best for the core of an electromagnet that must be switched on and off?
questions.x: Soft iron is easily magnetised and loses its magnetism when the current stops. Steel stays magnetised; copper and aluminium are not magnetic.

questions.q: An ideal transformer has 1200 turns on its primary coil, which is connected to the 240 V mains. Its secondary lights a 12 V, 24 W lamp at normal brightness. How many turns are on the secondary coil, and what is the current in the primary coil?
questions.x: Ns = 1200 × 12/240 = 60 turns. For an ideal transformer, power in = power out = 24 W, so Ip = 24/240 = 0.10 A. 2.0 A is the secondary current.
